transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is supply / door-interlock / control [random loss]. Next: Note the timing (a few seconds vs several minutes vs random) and whether it gets hot. Let me know what you find.

It's random, every few days, not a fixed time into the programme. No smell, sparks or tripping. It seems to happen more when I close the door gently, and the time stays on the display but the start indicator goes off and the fan and light stop, as if the door was opened.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door monitor / interlock microswitch (a mis-timed or failed monitor switch is the classic cause of a blown line fuse). If it blows the fuse, does it do so as soon as you switch on, or only when it starts to heat?
I haven't said anything about a blown fuse - it isn't blowing one, nothing trips. It just stops mid-cook with the time still showing, then carries on once I reopen and close the door.
Next: Check the wall socket with another appliance and the plug fuse where fitted. Let me know what you find.

Nothing else is affected, and the microwave heats normally otherwise, so I don't think the socket is the issue. It's a built-in so I can't easily get at the plug anyway. Any thoughts on the door side of things?

Yes, the door side is the most likely area: the fan and light stopping as if the door had opened, and it happening more when the door is closed gently, both suggest the door safety switches aren't always registering it as fully shut. On a microwave these switches must only be checked or replaced by a qualified repairer with the appliance isolated, never by opening the casing yourself. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door interlock / monitor microswitch (electrical start path). When you press the door-release button, does it feel normal, loose/floppy, or unusually stiff?
I'm not sure, I've never paid attention to how the release button feels. Is this something a Bosch engineer would need to look at, given I can't get the unit out of the housing?

Quite possibly: if it keeps cutting out, the repair needs a qualified microwave engineer (Bosch's own service or another qualified technician), as the inside of a microwave isn't safe for anyone else to open, and they can also take it out of the housing. Whether you need that visit depends on whether the fault carries on. Plug it back in and try a cup of water for a minute. Does the door latch and the microwave start normally now, or still not?

I haven't unplugged it, it's still installed and working, and it's screwed into the tall unit so I won't take it out. It heats normally apart from the occasional mid-cook stop. I'd pay for a Bosch engineer visit if that's the right next step, is it?

Quite possibly, but not just yet: a quick look at the door latch area first could show something simple like dirt or damage. If that turns up nothing, an engineer visit is the sensible route, since the inside of a microwave isn't safe for anyone else to work on and yours is built in. Next: The customer can visually inspect the accessible latch area. Let me know what you find.

I already cleaned some grease from around the door hooks and latch slots, but it still happened once since. The door looks very slightly lower on the handle side, though I can't be sure. No visible damage that I can tell.
Did it become harder to open over time, or did it suddenly stop opening?
Neither really - the door opens fine, it's not been hard to open or stuck. The only issue is the mid-cook stop every few days.
Next: Do not test internal interlock switches and never bypass an interlock. Let me know what you find.
